title: Regression Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE & R²
interviewAnswer: Regression metrics emphasize different error properties. RMSE punishes large errors; MAE is robust and in target units; MAPE fails near zero and weights relative errors unevenly; R² measures variance explained relative to a mean baseline.
why: Regression Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE & R² is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Regression metrics emphasize different error properties. RMSE punishes large errors; MAE is robust and in target units; MAPE fails near zero and weights relative errors unevenly; R² measures variance explained relative to a mean baseline. Scale-dependent vs scale-free metrics differ. Always compare with a baseline. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Forecast demand with MAE for typical unit error and WAPE/MASE for cross-series comparability rather than blindly using MAPE near zeros.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Regression Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE & R² have?
How would you validate Regression Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE & R² on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
